narrative.title: Densifying a Toll Gantry Corridor
narrative.scenario: A highway authority places k additional toll gantries between existing ones, at any positions along the corridor, to shrink the longest stretch a driver travels without passing a gantry. Choose the k placements to minimize that longest stretch. Report the optimized distance to two decimal places.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer N, an array stations of N sorted positions, and an integer K, the number of new stations to add.
narrative.outputFormat: The smallest achievable maximum distance between adjacent stations, rounded to two decimal places.
constraints: positions are given in strictly increasing order

complexity.optimalTime: O(N log M), where M is the initial maximum gap

testCases.explanation: Nine new stations slot one between each existing pair, halving every unit gap to 0.50.
The widest initial stretches are 23 and 24; two well-placed stations pull the worst stretch down to 14.

hintLevels: Level 1: The question 'with a max allowed gap of d, do K stations suffice' is monotonic in d, and d is a real number here.
Level 2: For a candidate d, each existing stretch of length L needs floor(L / d) new stations; sum them and compare with K.
Level 3: This is a continuous search: shrink the bracket on a fixed epsilon instead of integer bounds, and the floor-based counting already handles placements that serve two stretches at once.
